title: Should we buy a condo in Cyberjaya, where we rent, or an investment unit first?
excerpt: A married couple of 26 renting a three-bedroom Cyberjaya condo for RM1,300 plan to buy one there. Sean says keep renting cheaply, and buy an investment unit where rental demand is strong.

question.asker: From A, a viewer who wrote in by email
question.context: A and his wife are both 26, earn about RM12,000 a month between them, have no children yet and plan their first in one to two years. They have RM30,000 in emergency savings, no car loan and pay RM1,300 a month to rent a three-bedroom condo in Cyberjaya that they love. They are thinking of buying a Cyberjaya condo of about RM280,000 to RM300,000 to live in for five or six years, then renting it out when they upgrade to a landed home, ideally with no money down.
question.text: Should they stick to that plan, or buy an investment property first and keep renting?

answer.quote: Rent where we stay and to buy where we invest.
answer.summary: Buy an investment unit first, but not a Cyberjaya condo. Keep renting their home there, which is cheap for the space, and buy where rental demand is strong, checking recent transacted prices and nearby rents. A landed home can wait; it isn't easier with a baby anyway.

reasons.title: Cyberjaya's high-rises lag
reasons.body: Its infrastructure is complete and its landed homes sell well, but its condos haven't taken off and many end up at auction. Low rents there make renting better value than buying.

reasons.title: Keep your loan slots for investments
reasons.body: Many newlyweds tie up both 90% loans on a stretched landed home they later don't want to live in. Renting your home and buying an investment, then declaring its rent as income, lets you buy the next one sooner.

reasons.title: Two numbers decide rent or buy
reasons.body: Compare recent transacted prices in the area with the rent similar units fetch. Where the rent is a small fraction of the price, rent; where it can cover an instalment, consider buying.

reasons.title: A baby changes priorities
reasons.body: A reliable car matters more than an old car's savings, and a single-level home is easier with an infant than a landed house. Sean found a baby doesn't need much space, just an easy route from car to door.

actions: Keep renting your Cyberjaya home while it stays this good value.
Shortlist investment units in areas with strong rental demand, and check recent transacted prices and rents.
If you have the cash, prefer a subsale; if not, compare the channels for buying new, such as bulk purchases.
Check what EPF lets you withdraw towards a purchase or the loan under current rules.
Use a credit card for regular spending and pay it off in full each month to build your credit record.
caveat: If you'd rather give the family a home now, buying is a valid choice, but it changes your commitments for years; new landed homes near Kuala Lumpur now often cost over RM1 million.
sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's full English captions for Asking Sean #213. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. Figures are as the viewer and Sean stated them in June 2023. EPF withdrawal rules have changed since, so check the current ones.
